question: Does the current official publisher item page identify an article-level reuse license for Mallari et al. (2020), and what data gates remain?

publisherItemPage.finding: The current official journal item page for DOI 10.51453/2354-1431/2020/350 identifies the work as licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International. The page states that copyright belongs to the authors and that the journal receives a non-exclusive publication license. This is item-specific publisher metadata, unlike the prior ResearchGate file-level label.

publisherPdf.finding: The publisher-hosted PDF is the same cited article and contains its erratum, but the extracted PDF text does not itself show the CC BY-SA notice. The current item page provides the explicit license statement.

publisherPolicy.finding: The generic publication policy describes a required author copyright/licensing agreement at submission. It does not negate the current article-page CC BY-SA 4.0 notice.

licenseTerms.finding: The canonical license requires appropriate attribution, a license link, indication of changes, and ShareAlike for adapted material. Whether a particular Bangwit database projection is an adaptation needs separate legal review.

rightsDisposition.publisherDeclaredLicense: CC BY-SA 4.0 for the article, as stated on the current official journal item page.
rightsDisposition.previousFinding: The 2026-11-25 follow-up did not find an item-specific license notice on the publisher copy then reviewed. The current publisher item page now displays one; preserve the earlier artifact as a dated observation and use this recheck for current registry status.
reuseRequirements: link to the material and CC BY-SA 4.0 license
share adapted material under the same license
rightsDisposition.appProjection: No Bangwit projection is approved by this review. The source license is publisher-identified, but app/data ShareAlike compatibility and the accuracy of individual taxon records have not been reviewed.

unchangedEvidenceLimits.speciesClaims: The abstract lists 14 fish names, while a body passage describes five Cyprinidae plus ten species from other families. Several printed names are concatenated or malformed. This mismatch remains unresolved.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.museumDeposit: The article reports one representative preserved specimen per species group deposited at the Pampanga State Agricultural University Biology Museum, but provides no accession/catalog numbers or specimen-to-name crosswalk.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.localityAndTime: The paper names Barangays San Agustin and Dukma Paralaya but gives no collection dates, effort-standardized dataset, or taxon-by-site matrix. These are historical fishery-context claims, not current presence.
unchangedEvidenceLimits.reuse: The publisher-declared license resolves the article-level license metadata gap only. It does not resolve scientific identity, location, date, or app-projection compatibility.

nextActions: Keep the article and its fish list research-only until a source-faithful transcription and accepted-name review address the count conflict and malformed strings.
Do not infer dates, exact locations, or species-to-barangay assignments that the paper does not report.
Before any app projection, have a qualified reviewer assess attribution and ShareAlike compatibility for the intended data package.

sources.supports: Current official journal item page: author list, DOI, Candaba abstract, and item-specific CC BY-SA 4.0 notice with copyright/permission summary.
Official publisher PDF, including methods, fish inventory text, and erratum; no license notice in extracted PDF text.
Publisher general policy on author copyright/licensing agreement at submission.
Canonical CC BY-SA 4.0 deed and its attribution, change-indication, and ShareAlike conditions.
